mainTopic: The size of משה's altar: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue over 'קטן מהכיל' and over the altar's width and height
overview: The פסוק in מלכים א 8:64 says שלמה offered sacrifices in the middle of the courtyard because the copper altar was 'too small to receive' them. רבי יהודה reads this literally. רבי יוסי argues that שלמה once brought a thousand עולות on משה's small altar, so the Temple altar could not really have been too small. For him, 'too small' is a polite way of saying משה's altar was disqualified. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה is not convinced because he holds משה's altar was large. A ברייתא shows the dispute: רבי יוסי reads '5 by 5 אמות' as written, while רבי יהודה uses a גזירה שוה with יחזקאל's altar to measure from the center, making it 10 by 10. רבי יוסי uses the same word 'רבוע' instead to learn the height, comparing it to the incense altar, so משה's altar was 10 אמות tall. רבי יהודה objects that the 5-אמה courtyard walls would leave the כהן visible from outside. רבי יוסי answers with פסוקים tying the altar's height to the משכן's, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי contrasts Solomon's offerings on two altars
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי challenges the literal reading by comparing the thousand עולות שלמה brought on משה's altar with the offerings he brought at the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't the פסוק already say, 'A thousand burnt offerings did שלמה offer on that altar'? And about the בית המקדש it says, 'שלמה offered peace offerings to ה', twenty-two thousand cattle.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי attacks רבי יהודה's literal reading of 'too small to receive.' He brings two פסוקים to compare the two altars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes שלמה offering on משה's altar at גבעון. The second describes the dedication of the בית המקדש. רבי יוסי sets up these two numbers so he can compare them to the size of each altar in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it already stated? This introduces a פסוק that challenges the other view.
Burnt offerings, which are burned completely on the altar
The Eternal House, meaning the permanent בית המקדש
Peace offerings

phrases.english: But isn't it already stated:
"A thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer
upon that altar"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 3:4. 'That altar' is the copper altar משה made.

phrases.english: while regarding the Eternal House it says:
"And Solomon offered the sacrifice of peace offerings
which he offered to the Lord,
twenty-two thousand cattle"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוסי's side of the ברייתא against רבי יהודה's literal reading, which came earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's literal reading of 'קטן מהכיל'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a smaller altar could hold a thousand עולות, the bigger Temple altar should not have been too small.

steps.title: The math shows Moses' altar held more per cubit
steps.stepSummary: Comparing the number of offerings to the size of each altar, משה's altar carried more offerings for its size.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you work out the number of עולות against the number of אמות, this one is bigger than that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי finishes his challenge by doing the math. He divides the offerings by the size of each altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's small altar held a thousand עולות. Measured per square אמה, that is more than the Temple altar would have needed to hold at the dedication. So if the small altar was big enough, the larger Temple altar could not have been 'too small.'

keyTerms.meaning: Calculation
The count of אמות, meaning the size of the altar
This one is greater than that one

steps.confusionAlert: 'This is greater than that' does not mean משה's altar was physically bigger. It means משה's altar carried more offerings for each אמה of its size.

phrases.english: And when you arrive at the calculation of burnt offerings
and the number of cubits,
this is greater than that!
phrases.notes: He means the offerings on משה's altar were more per אמה than at the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from Step 1 by comparing the numbers with the altar sizes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the Temple's copper altar was physically too small
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה's altar held more offerings per אמה, so the larger altar should easily have held the dedication offerings.

steps.title: 'Too small' is a polite way of saying disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי offers his own reading: 'too small to receive' means the altar was disqualified, said politely.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what does 'too small to receive' mean? It is like a person who says to his friend, 'So-and-so is a dwarf,' and he means that person is disqualified from the Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: Having knocked out the literal reading, רבי יוסי gives his own explanation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dwarf may not serve in the בית המקדש, so calling a כהן a dwarf is a soft way of saying he is פסול. In the same way, calling משה's copper altar 'too small' is a soft way of saying it was no longer fit for use once the בית המקדש was dedicated.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what does it mean? This introduces a new explanation.
Too small to receive (מלכים א 8:64)
A dwarf
Disqualified from the Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, 'קטן מהכיל' is a polite way of saying משה's altar became disqualified. It does not describe its real size.

phrases.english: Rather, what is meant by "too small to receive"?
Like a person who says to his friend:
"So-and-so is a dwarf,"
and he means he is disqualified from the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the literal reading, רבי יוסי offers his own reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the פסוק as a polite expression
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means the altar was physically too small.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק politely means משה's altar was disqualified.

steps.title: Why isn't רבי יהודה convinced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can hold his view when רבי יוסי's argument seems strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? רבי יוסי is making a good point!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks for itself. It asks how רבי יהודה deals with רבי יוסי's convincing math, and this sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's argument looks strong. The גמרא wants to know what רבי יהודה would say back, since he still reads 'too small' literally.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying well, meaning his argument is convincing

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
Rabbi Yosei is saying well!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to רבי יהודה's view and asks how it survives רבי יוסי's challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's calculation seems to disprove it, so why does רבי יהודה keep it?

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds Moses' altar was large
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה follows his own view that משה's altar was big, so רבי יוסי's math does not work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, because he says the altar משה made was large.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבי יהודה starts from a different idea about the size of משה's altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's math only works if משה's altar was tiny. If משה's altar was large, a thousand עולות on it proves nothing about the Temple altar. So רבי יהודה can still say the Temple's copper altar really was too small.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, meaning consistent with a view he holds elsewhere
The altar that משה made

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
as he says: the altar that Moses made
was large.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sides agree משה's altar was small, so רבי יוסי's math should be decisive.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds משה's altar was large, so the comparison does not apply.

steps.title: The baraita on the size of Moses' altar begins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted. It opens with רבי יוסי's view that the 5-by-5 אמות of משה's altar should be read just as written.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'Five אמות long and five אמות wide.' The words mean exactly what they say. This is the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where רבי יהודה's view about the size of משה's altar comes from. It starts with רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי reads שמות 27:1 literally: the altar was only 5 by 5 אמות. That small size is what his math in Step 2 rests on. רבי יהודה's opposing view, that the altar was large, will follow in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The words are to be read as they are written

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument depends on how big משה's altar was. That is why the disagreement about the פסוק's measurements decides the argument about 'קטן מהכיל.'

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"Five cubits long
and five cubits wide"
The matters are as they are written.
These are the words of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the לטעמיה claim in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about the size of משה's altar
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שמות 27:1. It opens with רבי יוסי's literal reading, and רבי יהודה's view follows.

steps.title: רבי יהודה measures משה's altar from its center
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה compares the word 'רבוע' in משה's מזבח to the same word in יחזקאל's מזבח. Since יחזקאל measured from the center, משה's 5 אמות are also measured from the center.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The פסוק says 'square' here, about משה's altar, and it says 'square' there, about יחזקאל's altar. Just as there the measuring was done from the center, so too here the measuring was done from the center.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי יהודה's side. He says משה's מזבח was 5 אמות in each direction from its center, so it was 10 by 10 in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי read '5 by 5' just as written, but רבי יהודה uses a גזירה שוה to double it. This is the source for step 5: for רבי יהודה, משה's מזבח was big. So רבי יוסי's math about crowding does not work for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Square. This is the shared word that links the two מזבחות.
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
Here / there. These are the two פסוקים being compared.
From its center (middle)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
It is stated here: "square,"
and it is stated there: "square";
just as there he was measuring from its center,
so too here he was measuring from its center.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״רָבוּעַ״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״רָבוּעַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the ברייתא begun in step 6; gives רבי יהודה's opposing reading
steps.raayaObject: Step 5's claim that רבי יהודה holds משה's מזבח was large
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: גזירה שוה of 'רבוע' between שמות 27 and יחזקאל 43

steps.title: How do we know יחזקאל measured from the center?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that יחזקאל's מזבח was measured from its center.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, about יחזקאל's altar, how do we know it was measured from the center?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the base of רבי יהודה's comparison. It is setting up the next step, which brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's גזירה שוה only works if we already know that יחזקאל's מזבח was measured from the center. So the גמרא asks for proof of that fact.

keyTerms.meaning: And there, meaning in the other case
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the fact that step 7 relies on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that יחזקאל's מזבח was measured from the center

steps.title: 'To its four sides' shows measuring from the center
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in יחזקאל says 12 אמות 'to every side.' The words 'אל ארבעת רבעיו' show this means 12 in each direction from the center, not 12 by 12 in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the hearth is twelve cubits to every side.' Maybe it means only twelve by twelve in total? When the פסוק says 'to its four sides,' it teaches that he measures from the center.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about יחזקאל's מזבח. It raises a possible other reading and then rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You could read '12 אמות' as the total size, 12 by 12. But the extra words 'to its four sides' show that each side reaches 12 out from the middle, so the total is 24 by 24. This confirms the base that רבי יהודה needs.

keyTerms.meaning: The hearth, a name for the מזבח in יחזקאל
Direction or side
Or perhaps it is only, used to raise another possible reading
To its four sides

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the hearth shall be twelve cubits
in every direction."
Or is it only
twelve by twelve?
phrases.notes: Meaning 12 by 12 in total, not 12 out from the center on each side.

phrases.english: When it says: "to its four sides,"
it teaches that he is measuring from the center.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהָאֲרִיאֵל שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'אל ארבעת רבעיו' in יחזקאל 43:16 show measuring from the center

steps.title: רבי יוסי uses the word comparison for height
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי does use a גזירה שוה on 'רבוע,' but he applies it to the מזבח's height, not its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רבי יוסי do with this? When he learns the גזירה שוה, he learns it about the altar's height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי avoids רבי יהודה's comparison. It answers that רבי יוסי uses the word 'רבוע' to learn something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים use the word 'רבוע' to learn something. רבי יוסי keeps the width at 5 by 5 as written, and uses the comparison to learn the height instead. The next step brings a ברייתא to show this.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned or derived
Height

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei?
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: what does רבי יוסי do with רבי יהודה's comparison?

phrases.english: When he learns the verbal analogy,
it is regarding its height that he learns it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, כִּי גְּמִר גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוסי (step 6) handles רבי יהודה's גזירה שוה (step 7)
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the source: the same גזירה שוה is applied to a different measurement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seems to ignore the word 'רבוע'
steps.terutzMaskana: He uses 'רבוע' for height, so the width stays 5 by 5

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads the height of 3 אמות as written
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted. רבי יהודה says the 3-אמה height of משה's מזבח is meant just as written.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'And its height shall be three cubits' means just what it says. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove step 10. Its first part gives רבי יהודה's view on the height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the roles switch. רבי יהודה takes the height literally, the same way רבי יוסי took the width literally in step 6. This sets up רבי יוסי's opposing view on height.

keyTerms.meaning: Its height
The words are meant just as written

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"And three cubits shall be its height"
The matters are as they are written.
This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא that proves step 10
steps.raayaObject: Step 10's claim that רבי יוסי uses the גזירה שוה for height
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the height of משה's מזבח

steps.title: רבי יוסי makes משה's altar twice as tall as it is long
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי compares 'רבוע' to the מזבח הקטורת, which was twice as tall as it was long. So משה's 5-אמה מזבח was 10 אמות tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: It says 'square' here, about משה's altar, and it says 'square' there, about the incense altar. Just as there the height was twice the length, so too here the height was twice the length.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the ברייתא and proves step 10. רבי יוסי uses the word 'רבוע' to learn height, not width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח הקטורת was 1 by 1 אמה and 2 אמות tall. Using the same ratio, משה's 5 by 5 מזבח was 10 אמות tall. So רבי יוסי has already used up the גזירה שוה on height, and he keeps the width small.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense altar
Double, twice as much
Its length

steps.confusionAlert: The words are the same as in step 7, 'נאמר כאן רבוע ונאמר להלן רבוע,' but the 'there' is different! רבי יהודה compares to יחזקאל's מזבח, while רבי יוסי compares to the מזבח הקטורת.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: משה's מזבח was 5 by 5 wide and 10 tall. רבי יהודה: it was 10 by 10 wide and 3 tall. Each one uses the word 'רבוע' for a different measurement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It is stated here: "square,"
and it is stated there: "square";
phrases.notes: This time 'there' is the incense altar: שמות 30:2.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן – גּוֹבְהוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם כְּאׇרְכּוֹ,
phrases.english: just as there, its height is twice its length,
so too here, its height is twice its length.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״רָבוּעַ״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״רָבוּעַ״; מָה לְהַלָּן – גּוֹבְהוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם כְּאׇרְכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא; gives רבי יוסי's view on height, proving step 10
steps.raayaObject: Step 10: רבי יוסי applies the גזירה שוה to height
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: גזירה שוה of 'רבוע' between שמות 27:1 and שמות 30:2

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the courtyard walls were too low for a 10-amah altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה challenges רבי יוסי. The courtyard walls were only 5 אמות high. If the מזבח were 10 אמות tall, a כהן doing the עבודה on top would be seen by everyone outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to רבי יוסי: Doesn't the פסוק say the courtyard was 100 אמות long and 5 אמות high? Could it be that a כהן stands on top of the מזבח, holding the עבודה in his hand, and the whole nation watches him from outside?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה attacks רבי יוסי's claim from the last step that משה's מזבח was 10 אמות tall. He uses a פסוק about the height of the courtyard walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard curtains were 5 אמות high. A 10-אמה מזבח would rise far above them, so the כהן on top would be visible from outside. That would not be respectful to the עבודה, so רבי יהודה says the מזבח must really have been only 3 אמות tall, just as the פסוק says.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it already stated? (introduces a פסוק used to push back)
The courtyard around the משכן
Height
On top of the מזבח
The קרבן service the כהן performs

steps.confusionAlert: The '5 אמות' here is the height of the courtyard walls, not of the מזבח. Don't mix it up with the מזבח's 5-by-5 size from the previous step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יוסי, who just said the מזבח was 10 אמות tall.

phrases.english: But isn't it already stated:
"The courtyard, a hundred cubits
and the height five cubits, etc."

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר כֹּהֵן עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: Is it possible that a priest stands on top of the altar
with the service in his hand,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן is holding what he needs for the קרבן service.

phrases.english: and the whole nation sees him from outside?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's conclusion in Step 12 that משה's מזבח was 10 אמות tall.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that משה's מזבח was 10 אמות tall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The courtyard walls were only 5 אמות high, so a 10-אמה מזבח would leave the כהן fully visible from outside. That is not fitting for the עבודה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the altar was as tall as the Mishkan
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that a פסוק places the courtyard curtains 'by the משכן and by the מזבח,' which links the two: the משכן was 10 אמות tall, so the מזבח was too. He then begins a second פסוק about curtains of 15.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: Doesn't the פסוק say, 'The curtains of the courtyard and the screen of the courtyard gate, which are by the משכן and by the מזבח'? Just as the משכן was 10 אמות tall, so the מזבח was 10 אמות tall. And another פסוק says, 'Curtains of fifteen...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי defends his view. He brings his own פסוק that ties the מזבח's height to the משכן's height, and then starts quoting a second פסוק to answer the problem about the low courtyard walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the משכן and the מזבח together, so רבי יוסי reads them as equal in height: 10 אמות each. His second פסוק, about curtains of 15, is the start of his answer to רבי יהודה's question about the courtyard walls. The text stops in the middle of that quote, so the full answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtains that formed the courtyard walls
